versions.short: The bill would require the Environmental Protection Agency to change its rules within 180 days so that manufacturers of diesel vehicles and engines could temporarily turn off engine power reductions and shutdowns that the emissions system triggers when outside temperatures are at or below 20 degrees Fahrenheit, with the engine returning to normal operation once temperatures rise above that level. It would also let manufacturers permanently turn off those same functions for farm equipment and for vehicles mainly operated north of 59 degrees north latitude, based on commercial operation and maintenance and dispatch records. The bill would not waive any emissions standard under the Clean Air Act.
